articles.title: The US Struck Iran Over the Weekend. Iran Hit Back at a US Base in Kuwait. The Ceasefire Is Fraying.
articles.excerpt: Kuwait's air defenses intercepted missiles and drones on Monday morning as the three-month-old war produced its latest exchange of fire — even as both sides say a deal is close.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Buying Oil From Venezuela, Brazil, and Angola. The Strait of Hormuz Forced the Pivot.
articles.excerpt: With the critical shipping lane still closed three months into the US-Iran war, Indian refiners are diversifying away from the Middle East in what analysts call a structural shift.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Made It Mandatory to Use Indian-Made Solar Cells. It Has 40 GW of Manufacturing Capacity to Back It Up.
articles.excerpt: The ALMM mandate for solar PV cells takes effect today. No extensions, no exceptions — India's push to end dependence on Chinese solar imports enters its most consequential phase.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s Forex Reserves Have Fallen $47 Billion in Three Months. The RBI Is Spending Billions to Defend the Rupee.
articles.excerpt: From a record $728 billion in February to $681 billion in May — the central bank is burning through dollars as the Hormuz crisis, oil shock, and capital flight batter the currency.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Just Dumped $2.22 Billion in Indian Stocks in a Single Day. It Was the Largest Sell-Off in History.
articles.excerpt: MSCI's index rebalancing triggered record outflows and pushed NSE turnover past ₹2.87 trillion. Markets are expected to recover on Monday — but the structural headwinds remain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Sending 120 Deeptech Startups to France. It Is the Country’s Biggest Innovation Bet Yet.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026 will showcase chips, biotech, quantum, and clean energy ventures in Nice — timed to Modi’s G7 visit and the India-France Year of Innovation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Germany Just Approved 30 Initiatives to Recruit Indian Workers. It Reserved 90,000 Visas.
articles.excerpt: As America raises H-1B fees to $100,000, Berlin is marketing itself as the stable, predictable alternative for Indian tech talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Is Now Worth $965 Billion. Its Indian-Origin CFO Says the Demand Is 'Historic.'
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker has overtaken OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI startup. Krishna Rao is steering its finances as it approaches a trillion-dollar valuation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Said Vinesh Phogat Can Wrestle. The Federation Said She Could Not.
articles.excerpt: India's three-time Olympian was barred from Asian Games selection trials after a maternity break. The Delhi High Court and then the Supreme Court overruled the Wrestling Federation, saying motherhood is not a disability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Cleared Reliance of Fraud in a ₹447 Crore Market Manipulation Case.
articles.excerpt: India's apex court overturned SEBI's finding that Mukesh Ambani's company rigged Reliance Petroleum futures in 2007. It ordered SEBI to refund ₹250 crore. The ₹25 crore regulatory penalty stays.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Cancelled Its Biggest Medical Entrance Exam Over a Paper Leak. The Supreme Court Wants to Know Why It Keeps Happening.
articles.excerpt: The NEET-UG 2026 was scrapped after question papers were compromised on the eve of the test. The Supreme Court has demanded systemic reforms, a CBI probe is underway, and 24 lakh students are in limbo — again.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Scrapped All Cotton Import Duties Until October. The Textile Industry Says It Is Not Enough.
articles.excerpt: A 50-70 lakh bale shortfall in domestic cotton supply forced the government's hand. Industry leaders say the relief is welcome but spinning mills need to pass savings down the value chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TMC's Abhishek Banerjee Was Attacked With Bricks and Stones in Sonarpur. Five People Have Been Arrested.
articles.excerpt: The assault on Mamata Banerjee's nephew — who was visiting families affected by post-poll violence in West Bengal — has become a flashpoint in the state's bitter political transition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Diaspora Is Building a 20,000-Square-Foot Museum in Washington to Tell India's 11,000-Year Story.
articles.excerpt: The India Heritage Center, led by Atlanta-based Dr. Amitabh Sharma, will use VR, immersive galleries, and a 350-seat auditorium to present a civilisational narrative no American museum has attempted before.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Chief Trade Negotiator Lands in India Tomorrow. The Deal Is 99 Percent Done.
articles.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor says only the last 1 percent remains. A delegation arrives June 1 for four days of final talks that could seal the biggest bilateral trade pact in two decades.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Sent No Defence Minister to the Shangri-La Dialogue This Year. Everyone at the Forum Noticed.
articles.excerpt: For the first time since 2021, Beijing downgraded its delegation to researchers and mid-level officials — while India, the US, and Australia used the forum to announce new defence partnerships.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Australia Will Sit Down for Their Second Defence Ministers' Dialogue on Monday. Co-Production Is on the Table.
articles.excerpt: Rajnath Singh and Richard Marles will discuss co-development of defence equipment, military interoperability, and Indo-Pacific stability — six months after the inaugural dialogue in Australia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Said Green Card Applicants Must Leave the Country. A Week Later, It Said Never Mind.
articles.excerpt: A USCIS memo on adjustment of status has triggered panic among Indian H-1B holders. DHS walked it back within days, but immigration lawyers say the damage is already done.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India and IndiGo Are Cutting 250 Domestic Flights a Day Starting June. Fuel Costs Are the Reason.
articles.excerpt: India's two biggest carriers are slashing routes between Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and a dozen other cities as jet fuel prices surge and post-summer demand softens. NRIs planning trips home face fewer options and higher fares.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 300 Tourists Were Stranded 500 Feet in the Air Over Gulmarg. The Gondola Is Reopening Tuesday.
articles.excerpt: Asia's highest cable car malfunctioned last Sunday, trapping 320 people in 65 cabins for seven hours during heavy rain. The army, NDRF, and police pulled everyone out safely. An investigation is underway.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Hosted Every BRICS Foreign Minister in Delhi. The Agenda Was Bigger Than Anyone Expected.
articles.excerpt: From MSME technology access to alternative payment systems, India's BRICS chairship is shaping up as its most ambitious multilateral play in years. The leaders' summit is in September.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Bracing for Its Driest Monsoon in 11 Years. Farmers Are Already Worried.
articles.excerpt: The IMD now forecasts just 90 percent of normal rainfall this season. El Niño is building, the rupee is sliding, and two-thirds of the country still depends on rain-fed agriculture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian American Kid Just Won the Scripps Spelling Bee. Again.
articles.excerpt: Shrey Parikh, 14, from California shattered the spell-off record with 32 words in 90 seconds. The runner-up was also Indian American.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Myanmar's Junta Chief Turned President Is in India. He Wants Rare Earths and Legitimacy. Modi Wants to Counter China.
articles.excerpt: Min Aung Hlaing's five-day trip is his first foreign visit as president. For India, it is a chance to dilute Beijing's outsized influence on its eastern neighbour.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai's Dabbawalas Fed the City for 130 Years. Now Only 1,500 Are Left.
articles.excerpt: Remote work, app-based delivery, and rising costs are dismantling a logistics system that Harvard studied and Prince Charles admired.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Will Decide on Interest Rates This Week. The Rupee, Oil, and a Weak Monsoon Are All Working Against It.
articles.excerpt: Most economists expect the central bank to hold at 5.25 percent on June 5. But a growing minority thinks it should hike now before the situation gets worse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Tourist Shot a Local Youth in Kasol Over a Parking Dispute. He Then Chased Him Down the Street With a Pistol.
articles.excerpt: The shooting in Himachal Pradesh's most popular backpacker destination has renewed calls for a crackdown on violent tourists. Four suspects from Punjab have been arrested.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DK Shivakumar Will Be Sworn In as Karnataka CM on June 3. He Will Also Be India's Richest.
articles.excerpt: The Congress leader's declared assets of ₹1,413 crore place him ahead of Chandrababu Naidu and Thalapathy Vijay. All three of India's wealthiest chief ministers are now from the south.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Building Collapsed Near Delhi's Saket Metro Station. At Least Four People Are Dead.
articles.excerpt: A four-storey structure housing a coaching centre, cafes and offices came down without warning on Saturday evening. Rescue teams worked through the night.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Cut Fuel Export Duties. Exxon Says Oil Could Hit $160 Anyway.
articles.excerpt: The government eased levies on petrol, diesel, and ATF exports starting June 1. But global inventories are running out — and industry leaders say the worst is ahead.
articles.nri_angle: India imports over 85% of its crude oil. A sustained move to $150+ Brent would widen the current account deficit, weaken the rupee, and squeeze household budgets. NRIs sending remittances would see exchange rate pressure, while family members in India face higher transport and cooking fuel costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's Indian-Origin Mayor Just Launched His Own DOGE. Jeff Bezos Agreed With Him.
articles.excerpt: Zohran Mamdani's Commission on Government Efficiency is designed to do what Elon Musk's version never could: make government work without burning it down.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Set a 3-Month Deadline for High Courts to Deliver Judgments. India Has 5.49 Crore Cases Pending.
articles.excerpt: Bail orders must now be delivered the same day. If a reserved judgment is not pronounced in 90 days, the case can be reassigned to another bench.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Replaced Its Top Military Commander and Navy Chief on the Same Day. Here Is What Changes.
articles.excerpt: General Anil Chauhan retired after four decades in uniform. His successor inherits an unfinished revolution in how India fights wars.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Committed to Buying $500 Billion in American Goods. Economists Say the Math Does Not Add Up.
articles.excerpt: After Secretary of State Marco Rubio's India visit, trade experts and economists are questioning whether a $100-billion-a-year import target is feasible — or wise — for an economy already strained by a weak rupee and rising oil prices.
articles.nri_angle: A stronger US-India economic relationship supports the policy environment sustaining H-1B visas and bilateral business ties. But if the $500B commitment is perceived as one-sided, it risks fuelling political backlash that has already led to tariff escalations and immigration crackdowns affecting NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Pentagon Just Called India a 'Critical Anchor' in the Indo-Pacific. Then It Announced Javelin Co-Production.
articles.excerpt: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth used his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote to praise India's military modernisation, announce Javelin missile co-production, and demand that all Asian allies spend 3.5 percent of GDP on defence.
articles.nri_angle: A deepening US-India defence partnership — now including Javelin co-production — reinforces the geopolitical alignment that underpins H-1B policy, trade deals, and bilateral business ties. Defence-corridor manufacturing jobs in India could create new career pathways for dual-citizen professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The UK Foreign Secretary Is Visiting India Next Week. The Free Trade Deal They Signed Is Already in Trouble.
articles.excerpt: Yvette Cooper will meet S. Jaishankar to discuss the Russia-Ukraine war, Ebola, and trade. But London's new steel tariffs have created the first major friction point in an agreement that was supposed to be the UK's biggest post-Brexit prize.
articles.nri_angle: 1.9 million people of Indian heritage in the UK form the 'living bridge.' The trade deal promised easier business travel and reduced costs. UK steel tariffs threaten that promise and small business owners who import Indian goods face higher costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Power Grid Just Hit 270 Gigawatts of Peak Demand. Coal India Is Scrambling to Keep Up.
articles.excerpt: A record-breaking heatwave has pushed India's electricity consumption to an all-time high. Twenty-one power plants have critically low coal stocks. Blackouts are spreading from Gurugram to Bihar.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in India are hearing reports of load-shedding, water tanker shortages, and elderly relatives suffering without AC. The 270 GW demand peak and coal supply scramble expose the gap between India's tech-power ambitions and its grid infrastructure reality.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AUKUS Just Signed Its First Undersea Drone Pact. India Is Not Part of It.
articles.excerpt: The US, UK, and Australia will jointly develop unmanned underwater vehicles to protect seabed cables and project power. Deliveries begin in 2027. India — a Quad partner but not an AUKUS member — faces hard questions about its own undersea ambitions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin defence technology professionals work across the US, UK, and Australian defence sectors. India's exclusion from AUKUS undersea tech raises questions about NRI-connected defence innovation pipelines and India's strategic tier in the Indo-Pacific.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US and Iran Have Reached a Ceasefire Extension Deal on Paper. Neither Leader Has Signed It.
articles.excerpt: The 60-day memorandum would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the US naval blockade, and begin nuclear talks. Trump says he is in no rush. Iran says its Hormuz controls are permanent. India is watching its oil lifeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Just Launched a Trade Forum and Set a Deadline to Finish Their Free Trade Deal. The Thaw Is Real.
articles.excerpt: Commerce Minister Goyal led the largest Indian delegation ever sent abroad. Canada will send a trade mission to India later this year. Defence cooperation talks followed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Has Run Out of EB-2 Green Cards for Indians This Year. No More Approvals Until October.
articles.excerpt: The State Department confirmed that all EB-2 immigrant visa numbers for India-born applicants have been exhausted for FY2026, freezing final residency approvals for thousands of skilled professionals.
articles.nri_angle: The EB-2 freeze directly affects hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US on H-1B visas waiting for permanent residency.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Economy Grew Just 1.6 Percent Last Quarter. That Is Worse Than Anyone Expected.
articles.excerpt: A sharp downward revision to first-quarter GDP, driven by weaker consumer spending and the Iran war's inflationary toll, signals trouble ahead for hiring, mortgages, and the Indian professionals who depend on both.
articles.nri_angle: A slowing US economy directly impacts the 4.8 million Indian-origin Americans through hiring freezes, H-1B sponsorship pullbacks, higher mortgage rates, reduced remittance purchasing power, and a political environment less receptive to immigration reform. India received $129B in remittances in FY2025 — any US economic slowdown ripples directly to families back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seventy Percent of Karachi Has No Reliable Water. India's Indus Treaty Suspension Is Only Part of the Story.
articles.excerpt: Pakistan's financial capital faces a severe water crisis as the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance. But the real causes run deeper than geopolitics.
articles.nri_angle: The Indus Waters Treaty was a cornerstone of India-Pakistan relations that the diaspora followed closely. Its suspension signals a new phase in India's strategic posture, while the Karachi crisis exposes how infrastructure failures — not just geopolitics — drive water scarcity in the subcontinent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Quad Just Agreed to Build a Port in Fiji and Launch a Critical Minerals Pact. India Hosted It All.
articles.excerpt: The 11th Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi produced the grouping's first joint infrastructure project, a framework for critical minerals supply chains, and a maritime surveillance system — signalling the alliance is moving past photo-ops into operational territory.
articles.nri_angle: The Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework directly benefits Indian tech and manufacturing supply chains. For NRIs in tech and defence industries, alternative supply chains away from China reduce geopolitical risk. The energy security initiative addresses the Hormuz disruption that has raised fuel costs affecting remittance value and Indian market returns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Called the NEET Paper Leak 'Very Traumatic.' The Government Said Modi Is Personally Supervising.
articles.excerpt: Justices Narasimha and Aradhe told the NTA to learn from the UPSC, the CBI is probing a Maharashtra conspiracy ring, and a retest is set for June 21 — the second NEET cancellation in three years.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families abroad who send their children to take NEET for medical college admissions in India, the disruption is acutely painful. Many candidates travel to India specifically for the exam, arranging accommodation, coaching, and leave. A cancellation followed by a retest weeks later imposes enormous logistical and emotional costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The UAE Secretly Struck Iran Dozens of Times During the War. 3.5 Million Indians Live There.
articles.excerpt: A Wall Street Journal investigation reveals the Emirates carried out coordinated strikes on Iranian targets from the war's earliest days through the ceasefire — a far deeper military role than Gulf nations publicly acknowledged, with direct implications for the region's largest expatriate community.
articles.nri_angle: An estimated 3.5 million Indians live and work in the UAE — the largest Indian expatriate community in any single country. The revelation that the UAE was an active combatant, not a neutral bystander, directly affects the security calculus for Indian professionals and families who remained in the country throughout the conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is Down to the Last 1 Percent. A Delegation Arrives in Delhi Next Week.
articles.excerpt: Ambassador Sergio Gor says the deal could be signed within weeks. But the 'last 1 percent' is the hardest part — and the legal landscape under it has shifted.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chandrayaan-3 Has Won America's Highest Honor in Astronautics. ISRO Joins Jeff Bezos on the List.
articles.excerpt: The AIAA Goddard Astronautics Award recognizes the 2023 moon landing that made India the first nation to reach the lunar south pole. India's ambassador accepted it in Washington.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Signed a $629 Million BrahMos Missile Deal With Vietnam. Indonesia Is Next.
articles.excerpt: The defence secretary confirmed the deal at the Shangri-La Dialogue — making Vietnam India's second export customer for the supersonic cruise missile after the Philippines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Dropped Criminal Charges Against Gautam Adani. His Stock Surged 22% in a Month.
articles.excerpt: The DOJ moved to dismiss the bribery case. The SEC settled for $18 million. Adani Enterprises paid $275 million to resolve Iran sanctions allegations. The legal cloud that once wiped $150 billion off the Adani empire is lifting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
